topic: Yellow Leaves Were Hiding Their Color All Summer
creativeBrief:
Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers; state region, product and model scope naturally. Channel angle: familiar objects or observable natural events with a surprising true mechanism. Generate five declarative, concrete subject-first hooks; prefer 9–12 words without revealing the mechanism. Six story functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off; hard max 30. Keep voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. Aim for roughly 65–72 spoken words including the sign-off, without filler. Make mechanism begin at or after 7s and second reveal between 14s and 21s; each non-opening voiced clip must fit inside 5.8s of a six-second source after the incoming transition. Keep every spoken line easy to pronounce. No generic spoken CTA. Visual direction: photoreal Gemini still plus Google Flow six-second clip for each scene. Give each scene a distinct camera role; vary at least two of scale, angle, context, lighting and physical action between neighboring scenes. Start with the visible contradiction but save its cause for mechanism. Use a real object, ordinary hands or authentic setting; never invent a hazardous test or present generated media as a record of an actual event. Review stills, motion, 9:16 crop and factual visual details before importing MP4s. Packaging: use a curiosity-driven, slightly provocative YouTube title and a specific description with one topic-related question. The video must deliver what the title promises; do not exaggerate risk, savings or universal applicability.
Core fact: Green chlorophyll masks yellow and orange carotenoid pigments in many leaves during the growing season.
Second reveal: As chlorophyll breaks down in autumn, those colors become visible; some red colors also form through other pigment changes.
Opening shot: one branch with green, yellow and orange autumn leaves in natural daylight. Show it as a believable real-world shot, immediately legible in the first frame. Keep the cause for later scenes.
Fact boundaries: Different trees and weather produce different color patterns. Do not claim every yellow leaf had the same pigment mix or that red always was hidden.
